title: Contract ambiguity checklist and verbatim fixes
content:
Purpose: quick personal triage and ready-to-paste language when reviewing customer contracts. Focus = ambiguous conditional language, open-ended obligations, escape hatches we can propose, and suggested verbatim edits.

1) Quick triage checklist (first-pass, 60–90s)
- Is a deliverable, SLA, or security requirement defined by objective metrics or open ended terms like 'reasonable' / 'industry standard'? TAG as high risk.
- Are indemnities/cap restrictions mutual? If not, escalate.
- Does data residency / export have absolute language ('must stay in') vs. practical (we can offer region controls)? Note implications for Private vs Hosted.
- Look for 'in perpetuity', 'forever', 'irrevocable' on licenses or data retention: push localized retention windows.
- Unlimited liability or consequential damages carve-outs: flag and propose caps tied to fees.
- Audit rights: scope, frequency, notice, and cost allocation.
- Subprocessor language: who can appoint, notification cadence, customer approval?

2) Ambiguity patterns to watch (examples)
- 'Reasonable efforts' or 'commercially reasonable efforts' with no KPIs. Problem: subjective fallback.
- 'Confidential information' described by exceptions only (e.g., "not confidential if known to recipient"). Problem: reverse engineering and broad carve-outs.
- 'Customer data' vs 'Derived data' not defined. Problem: model improvement and telemetry disputes.
- 'Service interruption due to third party causes' with no commitment to mitigation. Problem: silent SLA degradation.

3) Verbatim replace-first-pass (copy/paste friendly)
- Replace: "Provider will use reasonable efforts to maintain availability."
  With: "Provider will maintain Service Availability >= 99.5% measured monthly, excluding Scheduled Maintenance and Force Majeure; see SLA section for credits."

- Replace: "Customer data may be used for analytics and to improve services."
  With: "Provider will process Customer Data solely to provide the Service and for anonymized telemetry aggregated at >k customers; Provider will not use Customer Personal Data to train models for third-party use without explicit written consent."

- Replace: "Provider may engage subcontractors to perform the Services."
  With: "Provider may engage Subprocessors provided (a) Provider gives Customer notice within 15 days of engagement and (b) Customer may object for reasonable security/compliance grounds; objections will be escalated to legal and reviewed in good faith."

- Replace: "Indemnified losses will include reasonable attorneys' fees."
  With: "Indemnified losses will include reasonable attorneys' fees and costs; damages will exclude punitive and consequential damages to the fullest extent permitted by law."

4) Priority ladder (how I triage during a negotiation)
- P0 (must fix in initial redline): unlimited liability, data residency absolute language, carve-outs for customer IP, irrevocable data transfer.
- P1 (strongly prefer to fix): ambiguous SLA/availability, broad audit rights without limits, unclear subcontractor approval, retention 'forever'.
- P2 (can compromise later): warranty language that duplicates product disclaimers, non-critical indemnity symmetry, minor notice periods.

5) Concession playbook (phrases to offer when we need to give ground)
- If asked to remove a cap: "We can consider an increase in the liability cap tied to a term commitment or a higher support tier (Dedicated / Enterprise)."
- If asked to accept broader audit rights: "We accept audit rights if audits are scheduled with 30 days' notice, limited to once per 12 months, and conducted during business hours with our security rep present; costs borne by Customer unless material noncompliance is found."
- If asked to remove export restrictions: "We can allow specific export to XXX country if Customer provides written proof of lawful basis and accepts additional security controls and data processing addendum."

6) Short negotiation scripts (for quick syncs with CS/AE or in redline comments)
- On SLA: "We hear the need for reliability; our SLA already commits to [99.5%]. For higher criticality, we recommend Dedicated capacity + a 99.9% SLA option — happy to put pricing and SLO into an amendment."
- On data use: "We can offer an explicit opt-out for training and a 'no-PII' clause for telemetry. If you need model retraining access, let's scope a JRA (Joint Research Agreement) with explicit boundaries."
- On liability caps: "Our standard cap is tied to 12 months' fees. If you need a higher cap, we can do so for an enterprise commitment or purchase of our premium SLA."

7) Redline snippets for hard calls (short, assertive)
- Audit limitation: "Audits limited to once per 12 months, three business-days' notice, duration no longer than two business days, and limited to systems relevant to the alleged noncompliance."
- Data retention: "Provider will retain Customer Data only as necessary to provide the Service and as required by law; otherwise, Customer may request deletion and Provider will delete within 30 calendar days."

8) Edge-case reminders (notes to self)
- If customer is in highly regulated industry (finance, healthcare): confirm KMS/HSM options and data plane isolation before promising region controls.
- For on-prem/private: Many clauses can be negotiated because infra and physical controls change risk profile — emphasize installation and runbook clauses.
- If customer asks for unlimited export or 'transfer to any affiliate': require auditing and SSAE-type attestation from the receiving party or deny.

Open questions / todo
- Draft a short 'customer-facing' paragraph for AE to use when customers ask about "do you train on customer data?" (Make version for hosted vs private).
- Pull together common countersigned language across last 12 closed deals (use Legal ops report CONFLUENCE-1234).

Notes-to-self: keep this file focused and short. When I see repetitive asks, extract into a canonical "Customer redline playbook" under shared_drives/legal. This is the scratchpad for ad-hoc replies.

Examples of recent odd clauses I saw (context snippets)
- "Provider will indemnify Customer for any loss arising from model outputs that cause reputational damage." -> push to 'no-outputs-warranty' plus carve-out for malicious customer prompts.
- "Customer may terminate for convenience with immediate effect" -> counter with 30 days notice and termination charges if committed discounts applied.

End of notes.
